title: Third-Party Telemetry Minimization & Sampling Exhibit
body:
Exhibit: Telemetry Minimization and Sampling for Third-Party Integrations

Purpose
This Exhibit supplements the Data Processing Agreement and Security Addendum between Redwood Inference ("Provider") and the Vendor ("Vendor") and sets forth minimum requirements and operational controls for telemetry collection, sampling, minimization, retention, and evidentiary practices applicable to telemetry generated as a result of Vendor integrations with Provider services ("Telemetry"). The Exhibit prioritizes privacy, security, and reproducibility of incidents while preserving necessary operational observability.

Scope
Applies to: (a) any telemetry (metrics, logs, traces, debug artifacts, aggregate usage statistics) that references or is derived from customer requests, request metadata, or system behavior resulting from interactions with Redwood-hosted inference; (b) telemetry produced by Vendor components running in Provider managed, Dedicated, or Private deployments; and (c) telemetry exported to Vendor-controlled systems for monitoring, analytics, or debugging.

Definitions
- Telemetry: Observability data including logs, metrics, traces, synthetic checks, profiling data, crash dumps, and diagnostic artifacts.
- Identifying Telemetry: Telemetry that contains, directly or indirectly, personal data, prompt/query text, full or partial model outputs, or persistent identifiers (e.g., user_id, account_id, device_id, IP).
- Minimized Telemetry: Telemetry that has been transformed to remove or irreversibly pseudonymize Identifying Telemetry while preserving necessary signal for the stated purpose.
- Sampling Event: A record describing the criteria and timing for selecting a subset of requests or telemetry for retention in full fidelity for debugging or analytics.

Core Requirements
1) Purpose Limitation and Collection Minimization- Vendor shall only collect Telemetry necessary for the explicit, documented purposes described in the integration design (performance monitoring, SLA verification, security detection, billing reconciliation). Any collection beyond those purposes requires Provider prior written approval.- Telemetry classified as Identifying Telemetry must be minimized at source: redact prompt text and model outputs, pseudonymize identifiers using a one-way hash salted with a Provider-provided per-integration salt, or convert to aggregate counters where feasible.

2) Sampling Policy and Acceptable Rates- Default sampling rates for Vendor-collected Telemetry are as follows unless otherwise agreed in writing:
  - Error traces and crash dumps: 100% for the first 7 days after deployment of new code; thereafter 20% by default.
  - Latency p95/p99 metric collection: 100% for aggregation metrics; raw traces sampled at 5% at peak traffic, 1% at low traffic.
  - Prompt/response capture for debug: 0.1% without explicit Provider approval.
  - Security-relevant events (anomalous auth failures, rate limit breaches): 100% capture for 30 days, then subject to minimization/aggregation.
- Vendor must implement deterministic sampling for debugging reproducibility (e.g., hash-based sampling keyed by request identifiers) and record sampling decision flags for every Telemetry item. Sampling rules must be stable and configurable via the Provider console or integration config.

3) Retention, Aggregation and Deletion- Retention windows: Minimized Telemetry: maximum 365 days unless otherwise restricted by law or customer requirement. Full-fidelity Identifying Telemetry retained for debugging: maximum 30 days unless an exception is granted by Provider security/privacy team.- Aggregated aggregates (e.g., daily request counts per endpoint) may be stored longer but must not contain Identifying Telemetry.- Vendor must provide mechanisms for expiring and permanently deleting Telemetry on the retention schedule and support Provider-initiated immediate deletion requests for specific datasets.

4) Access Controls and Encryption- Telemetry at rest and in transit must be encrypted with industry-standard algorithms (TLS 1.2+ for transit, AES-256 or equivalent for rest).- Access to raw Telemetry that contains Identifying Telemetry must be restricted to a minimum personnel set. Vendor must maintain an access log and quarterly attestation of least privilege.

5) Evidence, Auditability and Logs of Decisions- For each Sampling Event, Vendor must persist a Sampling Decision Log that contains: timestamp, active rule identifiers, hashed request keys used for deterministic sampling, and a cryptographic HMAC over the log entry (keyed using a Provider-shared HMAC key or a mutually-agreed KMS key). Sampling Decision Logs must be retained for 180 days and made available to Provider auditors on request.

6) Pseudonymization and Re-identification Controls- Any reversible mapping used by Vendor to re-link pseudonyms to original identifiers is strictly prohibited unless explicitly authorized by Provider in writing and locked under a joint control KMS with rotation policies. Vendor must document pseudonymization algorithms and prove they are one-way for the selected datasets.

7) Incident Response and Forensics Support- In the event of a suspected telemetry leak or unauthorized access:
  - Vendor shall immediately (within 4 hours) notify Provider security primary alias and preserve forensic copies of relevant Telemetry segments.
  - Provider may request a temporary retention pause for specific Telemetry subsets to support an investigation; Vendor will comply for up to 14 days with documented justification.

8) Sampling Exception and Full-Fidelity Capture- If Provider requests full-fidelity capture for a bounded investigation or product onboarding trace, Vendor must:
  - Accept a signed scope and purpose document from Provider authorizing full-fidelity retention,
  - Apply strict access controls, and
  - Timebox retention to the agreed period (not to exceed 90 days without explicit Provider approval).

9) Compliance, Attestations and Penalties- Vendor shall provide quarterly attestations that sampling and minimization controls are in effect and provide random sample artifacts for verification. Material breach of the obligations in this Exhibit (e.g., persistent capture of prompt text without minimization, failure to honor deletion requests, unauthorized re-identification) shall be considered a breach under the primary agreement and may trigger remediation plans, audit rights, damages, or termination per the Agreement.

Operational Implementation Notes (non-exhaustive)
- Implement SDK hooks at the RPC boundary to remove prompt fields prior to any telemetry emission.
- Use salted HMAC of the request_id for stable sample-key generation.
- Record and surface a sampling_flag header in traces so Provider-side tooling can correlate traces across sampled/un-sampled datasets.
- Provide a lightweight JSON manifest describing the telemetry schema and sample rates per endpoint; publish it as part of the integration config.

Evidence Package Requirements
For audits or security reviews Vendor will provide:
- Sampling Decision Logs for the requested period (as CSV or NDJSON),
- Representative minimized telemetry samples and a record of the minimization transformation used,
- Access logs showing who accessed raw telemetry and when,
- Proof of encryption keys and rotation policies (KMS URIs or HSM descriptions).

Change Management
This Exhibit is expected to evolve. Vendor must notify Provider of any telemetry schema changes, sampling algorithm changes, or retention policy changes at least 30 days prior to implementation. Emergency changes for security fixes may be implemented with retrospective notice and justification.

Signatures
This Exhibit is intended to be attached to the DPA/Security Addendum and become binding when signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

Acknowledgement and Contact
Questions or requests for exceptions should be routed to security@redwood.ai with the subject line: "Telemetry Exhibit Exception Request: <Vendor Name>".

Annex A: Example Sampling Decision Log Record (NDJSON line)
{"timestamp":"2026-01-07T14:12:03Z","rule_id":"latency-sample-v1","request_hash":"a3f5c8...","sampled":true,"hmac":"h1a2b3c..."}

Annex B: Minimal Redaction Examples
- Original log line (DO NOT STORE IN PRODUCTION): REQUEST: {"user_id":"u-12345","prompt":"What is my SSN?","response":"..."}
- Minimized stored line: {"user_hash":"h-9a8b7","prompt_redaction":"[redacted]","response_features":"length=24,contains_digits=false"}

Revision History

2025-12-10: Added deterministic sampling and HMAC requirement (R. Singh)
2026-01-15: Clarified retention windows and annex examples (M. Lopez)

End of Exhibit.
